endorsements.quote: As conducting RCTs can be challenging, other study designs that provide valid evidence for clinical, industry, and public health decision makers should be considered when assessing the safety of launching an AI medical technology.

To guarantee, ethical conduct is performed across the study phases, collaborations between industry and patients (via participatory action research study designs and advocacy groups), health care professionals (via academic institutions), and governments (via regulatory agencies) are encouraged.

unlisted_practices: Require AI developers to demonstrate biological-psychological, economic, and social safety and value for patients, health care professionals, industry, and government using a Go or No-Go checklist before launching an AI medical technology.
Conduct a phase 1 quantitative study establishing that the AI tool is as safe and efficacious as or more than the standard approach before launch.
Conduct a phase 2 quantitative study capturing the long-term benefits and risks of the AI tool.
Conduct a phase 3 qualitative study to uncover concerns and biases and understand the social context of quantitative results.
Submit summarized results of phase 1 to 3 studies to the national health care regulatory agency for review and feedback before launch.

screen.reason: The paper introduces a conceptual framework (BPES) and checklist/phased trial approach to guide deployment go/no-go decisions for AI in healthcare; it does not report an empirical evaluation.
